response:
No, the statement is not true for every artificial neural network.

In a typical feedforward neural network, each neuron in a layer only connects to the neurons in the next layer, not to all of them. This is because the connections between neurons are typically one-to-many, meaning that each neuron in one layer can send a signal to multiple neurons in the next layer. This is a fundamental property of feedforward networks, which are the most common type of artificial neural network.

However, there are other types of neural networks, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), that do not follow this rule. In RNNs, each neuron in a layer can connect to neurons in the same layer, as well as to neurons in previous layers, allowing the network to maintain a sense of temporal context. In CNNs, each neuron in a layer can only connect to neurons in the same layer, but the connections are organized in a way that allows the network to process images in a spatially-structured manner.
